title: fix(ci): trigger Build Docs on what the site build actually consumes
body:
Fixes #8647

## What was wrong

The `docs` job decided whether to build the site by diffing against `apps/site/` and `content/` only. Those are the site's **output** surface. Its **input** surface is the whole workspace closure turbo builds before `next build` runs at all — so a pull request touching only `packages/**` skipped the build and still reported `success`, in seconds. A skipped build and a passed build are the same green to every reader downstream, and cards in this lane had begun leaning on that green as their Turbopack evidence.

⭐ Scope note, so the record stays accurate: this **never** let an unbuilt site reach `main`. The `merge_group` leg already builds the site on every merge (the early return that guarantees that is untouched here). What the pull-request filter cost was **early** detection, not the final gate.

## The trigger, and why it is derived rather than curated

A hand-written include list decays silently in exactly the direction this card is about — add a dependency, forget the workflow, and the gate quietly narrows again with nothing red anywhere. So the pathspec is derived from three sources, and the pin re-derives all three on every pull request:

1. **one entry per workspace package in the site's build closure** — the package-manifest graph reached from `@object-ui/site` over `dependencies`, `devDependencies` and `peerDependencies` on the `workspace:` protocol, which is the graph turbo walks for `^build`. Measured against turbo itself rather than assumed: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/site' --dry=json` reports **31 entries** — these 30 packages plus the site. One of them (`packages/test-support`) declares no `build` script, so **30 tasks** actually execute.
2. **one entry per root-level input `turbo.json` declares for the `build` task** (the `$TURBO_ROOT$/...` entries), because turbo names them as things a build's output depends on.
3. **the four workspace manifests**, since they decide which versions of everything the build resolves.

Plus **one deliberate, non-derived entry: this workflow file.** A pull request that edits the job should be validated by the job it edits — otherwise the acceptance evidence for a change to this gate is the very 13-second green the change exists to remove. It is not `.github/` wholesale, and the pin asserts an unrelated workflow still skips.

## Cost — measured, not estimated

Priced by replaying **this exact pathspec** against each of the **400 most recent merged pull requests** (squash commits on `main`, one per pull request), using the same `git diff --name-only BASE...HEAD -- pathspec` the step runs. Measured on `2596b1b85`, the tip this branch was cut from:

| trigger set | fires on | newly paying |
|---|---|---|
| the old list (`apps/site/` + `content/`) | 54 / 400 (13.5%) | — |
| **this pull request** | **281 / 400 (70%)** | **227 / 400 (56.8%)** |
| every `packages/` + `apps/` + `examples/` | 341 / 400 (85.2%) | +15 points |
| this list plus all of `scripts/` | 333 / 400 (83.2%) | +13 points |
| every pull request | 400 / 400 | +30 points |

Site build cost measured on the dev container: **2m28s** with an empty turbo cache (30 tasks, `--concurrency=2`); the card measured 3m16s on its own machine. The workflow's own record puts this job's whole verdict path at 4m26s on a `merge_group` build, against a `timeout-minutes: 15` ceiling — so the ceiling keeps roughly 3x headroom and is not touched here. The job runs in parallel with the other eight, so the cost is runner minutes rather than critical path.

⛔ **One narrowing was priced and declined.** Excluding tooling files (`__tests__`, `__mocks__`, `__benchmarks__`, `*.test.ts`) under the closure packages would take it to 238 / 400 — a further 11 points — and it is sound today, because every published build program in this repository excludes those directories and a repo-wide gate enforces that. It is declined anyway: this gate's entire defect class is **under-firing silently**, and an exclusion is a second thing that has to stay true for the defect not to recur. Over-firing costs minutes and is visible; under-firing costs the whole point of the check and is invisible. That asymmetry decided it.

Also excluded, for the same measured reason they buy nothing: the 11 workspace packages outside the closure, and `scripts/` beyond the entries turbo itself declares.

## ⭐ The firing control — a green run is not evidence here

The acceptance evidence had to be a shape that **previously reported green-without-building and now actually builds**. Both versions of the decision step were extracted and executed against identical throwaway git repositories, with `bash -e` and the three expressions GitHub substitutes:

| diff shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the shape the card was filed on — `packages/types/**` only, 4 files | `should_run=false` | **`should_run=true`** |
| a module-cycle change in `packages/core` (the objectui#8344 class) | `should_run=false` | **`should_run=true`** |
| a lockfile bump | `should_run=false` | **`should_run=true`** |
| **this pull request's own shape** — the workflow plus a `scripts/__tests__` pin | `should_run=false` | **`should_run=true`** |
| a change confined to a package outside the closure | `should_run=false` | `should_run=false` |
| a docs-only change | `should_run=true` | `should_run=true` |

The fourth row means this pull request is itself a live firing control: under the old step it would have taken the seconds-long green as its own evidence; under the new one, the `Build Docs` check on this head is a real Turbopack build. Observed on the first push: `Build Docs` still `in_progress` after `Build & E2E` had already completed.

## The pin

`scripts/__tests__/docs-build-trigger.test.ts` — 72 test cases, ~3s.

⭐ It does not grep the pathspec. It extracts the step's `run:` script verbatim, substitutes the three expressions, and **executes it with `bash -e`** (GitHub's own default shell for `run:` on Linux) against throwaway git repositories, asserting the `should_run` value the step actually writes to `GITHUB_OUTPUT`. That is what lets it tell **"built and passed" from "skipped"**, which the check itself cannot: `should_run` is the switch every later step in the job is gated on. The set of substituted expressions is itself pinned, so a new expression cannot leave the harness silently unfaithful.

What it holds:

- the firing control above, as a test;
- **drift guard 1** — every package in the re-derived closure must make the real step answer `true`, checked one package at a time, so an entry that is misspelled, wrongly quoted or shadowed fails here rather than in production;
- **drift guard 2** — every root input `turbo.json` declares, and every manifest, likewise;
- **the negative set is derived too** — `all workspace packages − closure` must still skip, so a package that later joins the closure moves between the two sets on its own instead of leaving a stale expectation behind. This is what keeps a future widening honest about not having become "every pull request";
- the `merge_group` early return and the fail-open branch, both asserted behaviourally;
- ⛔ **the job is still named `Build Docs`**, and neither trigger carries a `paths` filter. It is a required status check on the merge-queue ruleset: a required context that stops reporting is not a stricter gate, it is a repository where nothing can merge. Every remedy here keeps the job reporting on every pull request exactly as it does today.

## The guide sentence this change made false

The CI/CD pipeline guide's row for this job said it "skips the build when nothing under `apps/site/` or `content/` changed". This branch makes that false, so this branch fixes it — one line, in the job table, well clear of the two regions the other card on that page is editing.

⛔ The replacement does **not** restate the path set. It says what the set is derived from and what re-derives it, and states no live count at all — because a path list or a count copied into prose is stale the moment the closure moves, which is precisely the defect [#8629](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/8629) landed against on this very page today. It keeps the history (the filter used to name the site's output surface only) and the scope note (the queue leg always built, so what was lost was early detection).

## The one coupled change

The command-parity pin for the CI/CD guide scrapes `scripts/*.mjs` out of a job's `run:` bodies and demands the guide document each one. Four of turbo's declared root inputs are `scripts/*.mjs` paths, so as **pathspec arguments** they read to that scraper as commands the `docs` job runs — it went red asking the guide to document four gates that job never executes, which would have been a false statement on the page.

Fixed at the parser, not by writing the false statement: a **shell-single-quoted** path is an argument, not a command. That matches how this repository already writes path lists everywhere (every `on.paths:` entry is quoted; every invocation is not). It carries its own control in the same file — one assertion that the quoted pathspec entry is excluded, one that an unquoted `node scripts/...` invocation in the same job is still counted, so the exclusion cannot silently swallow every real gate and leave both directions green.

## Premises checked

All four premises in the dispatch held, plus:

- ✅ the `Check for docs changes` step is live and its `should_run` guards **exactly eight** later steps in the job (counted: Corepack, pnpm version, Node setup, Turbo restore, install, Build Site, the carriage census, Turbo save — the pin asserts at least eight and that `Build Site` is one of them);
- ✅ the `merge_group` early return is live, correct and **untouched** — asserted behaviourally, not by inspection;
- ✅ the queue leg already builds on every merge, so this defect never let an unbuilt site reach `main`. Neither this body nor the pin claims otherwise;
- ✅ the card's corroborating readings were not re-measured, and the trigger choice does not depend on them. The uncached build was re-measured only because the cost decision does.

## Verification

Run on the merged head, after `origin/main` (carrying the guide's own re-pointing card) was merged in:

- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/` — 138 files, 4077 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed;
- the three pins that read this change directly — the new trigger pin, the command-parity pin for the guide, and the docs-links workflow pin — 153 passed together, including the pins that landed on that page today;
- `pnpm run type-check:scripts` — clean, and the new pin is genuinely inside that program (confirmed by counting it in `tsc --listFiles`, not assumed);
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the changed `scripts/__tests__` files — clean;
- `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` — links valid across 17 scan roots; `check:doc-fences`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:action-ref-convention`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:entry-guard`, `type-check:coverage`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:lint-rule-coverage`, `check:comment-mask-corpus` — all exit 0;
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — 5 files changed, 0 of them published source or a moved published contract, **no changeset owed**;
- `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/site'` — 30/30 tasks succeed on this branch, so the widened trigger fires into a build that passes.

Drafted by an agent seat, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`. ⛔ Left as a draft deliberately; the PM seat does the landing.
